subject: Annual commit proposal — usage tiers and flexible ramp (LumenHealth)
messages:
From: Anna Torres <anna@lumenhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: LumenHealth Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual commit tiers for hosted API

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking the time last week to walk us through the Redwood Hosted API. Procurement wants a single-page overview of the committed tiers you mentioned — plus the negotiation levers we can use if usage ramps slower than expected. Our core asks:

- Clear per-token price at each tier (starter / growth / enterprise) and the corresponding discount vs list.
- Minimum annual commitment billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly true-up).
- Options for credits/refunds if we underutilize vs true-up clauses.
- Any ramp/fallback allowances for pilot months (we have a Jan product launch and expect a big ramp from Feb–May).

Can you share a proposal we can review internally this week? I can loop in legal once we have a high-level commercial term sheet.

Thanks —
Anna Torres
Head of Product Integrations | LumenHealth
anna@lumenhealth.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: none
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Torres <anna@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring annual commit tiers for hosted API

Hi Anna — great question and thanks for the clarity on timeline. Attached is a single-page commercial summary plus a short projection we ran against your Q4–Q1 forecast (see LumenHealth_pricing_summary_v1.pdf and usage_projection_q4_q1.csv). High-level proposal below; happy to iterate.

Proposed annual commit tiers (Hosted API, usage-based per-token billing):

- Starter: 250M tokens/year commit (good for pilots / limited production)
  - Effective price: $0.00095 / token (≈ 15% off list rate)
  - Billing: quarterly true-up with 30-day invoice terms
  - Ramp allowance: first 2 months pilot counted at 50% of actual for true-up calculation

- Growth: 1.5B tokens/year commit (launch + steady growth)
  - Effective price: $0.00072 / token (≈ 25% off list rate)
  - Billing: monthly usage reporting + quarterly true-up
  - Ramp allowance: first 3 months counted at 75% of actual; one-time 5% billing credit if monthly usage < 60% of forecast for first 3 months

- Enterprise: 8B tokens/year commit (scale + SLOs)
  - Effective price: $0.00049 / token (≈ 35% off list rate)
  - Billing: monthly, with annual true-up and committed minimums enforced
  - Ramp allowance: custom ramp schedule — we recommend a 6 month phase with a linear ramp to committed monthly run-rate

Optional commercial flex:
- Excess usage billed at list-discounted overage price (we can cap overage rate for first 6 months by agreement).
- Underutilization: standard true-up applies; however we can offer a partial crediting mechanism for first-year deals (up to 10% of committed value convertible to support/credits).
- Exit/fallback: ability to step down one tier at the next annual renewal with a 60-day notice.

Attachments in this thread: pricing summary PDF and a small usage projection we ran against the numbers you shared.

Next steps: If that looks directionally right, I can send a one-page term sheet and a DocuSign link for signatures. If procurement/legal want different billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly), flag it and we can include that in the term sheet.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Rachel.Kim@redwood.com | (415) 555-0201

Attachments: LumenHealth_pricing_summary_v1.pdf, usage_projection_q4_q1.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Annual commit proposal — pricing / credits options for LumenHealth

Looping in with quick internal feedback — keeping it tight for legal/commercial:

- Starter tier looks fine as-is for pilot — provides runway without heavy discounting.
- For Growth tier, given LumenHealth's TAM and reference value, we should be prepared to move an additional 2% discount on list for a 2-year commit (gives them predictability).
- For Enterprise-scale asks (8B), ops wants a clear SLA and fallback rule: if we hit sustained 90th percentile latency beyond SLO for >72 hours, automatic temporary crediting applied and routing to dedicated capacity. Add that to term sheet.
- On credits: finance prefers partial crediting (convertible to prepaid consumption credits) rather than cash refunds. That preserves ARR profile.

Marissa — can you confirm the maximum convertible-credit we can offer on a first-year pilot for a new strategic account? I'm thinking 10% of committed value as Rachel proposed, but want to ensure it's acceptable for revenue recognition.

Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Annual commit proposal — pricing / credits options for LumenHealth

Confirmed — finance will approve the following commercial guardrails for this deal:

- First-year convertible credit: up to 10% of committed ARR; credits are non-refundable and must be used toward Redwood services within 12 months. This is classified as contra-revenue and requires a signed MSA and commitment schedule to qualify.
- 2-year extended commit discount: additional 2% off list (applies only to Growth tier and above) if LumenHealth signs a 24-month commitment with annual true-up.
- Ramp allowances: pilot ramp credit rules (50% for first 2 months or 75% for first 3 months) are acceptable, but any extended ramp must be pre-approved and tied to a mutually agreed forecast doc.
- Overage cap: we can cap overage rate for first 6 months at the discounted overage price, after which standard overage rates apply.

I'll draft the finance-approved clause language and drop into the term sheet. Rachel — include the MSA draft with the commercial schedule so legal can start a parallel review.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Finance, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
